location.zh: Brightway 照明公司，產品展示間

goal.en: Clear up a cultural misunderstanding with a visiting client.
goal.zh: 化解和來訪客戶之間的文化誤會。

background: modern lighting showroom with rows of glowing pendant lamps, sample fixtures on white display shelves, a small round meeting table with two chairs, polished concrete floor, late morning

intro.en: Mr. Becker, procurement manager for Alpenhaus Hotels, has flown in from his company's head office overseas to review Brightway's offer.
intro.zh: 阿爾彭豪斯飯店集團的採購經理貝克先生，從海外總部飛來審查 Brightway 的報價。

intro.en: Heads up, Kai. People say he's very direct. Don't take it personally.
intro.zh: 先提醒你，凱。聽說他講話非常直接，別往心裡去。

lines.en: Good morning. Your proposal is good, but there are two errors on page four.
lines.zh: 早安。你們的提案不錯，但第四頁有兩個錯誤。

choices.en: Thank you for pointing that out. I'll correct them today. Which parts did you notice?
choices.zh: 謝謝您指出來，我今天就會修正。您注意到的是哪些地方？
choices.tip: 對方直接指出錯誤時，道謝並詢問細節，是最專業的回應。

choices.en: Errors? Oh... I'm so sorry. You don't like our proposal at all, do you? We failed you.
choices.zh: 錯誤？噢……真的很抱歉。您一點都不喜歡我們的提案，對吧？我們讓您失望了。

lines.en: Not like it? I just said it was good. I only mentioned two small errors.
lines.zh: 不喜歡？我剛剛才說很好。我只是提到兩個小錯誤。

story.en: Mr. Becker spends five minutes reassuring you instead of reviewing the offer. He is not sure why you are so upset.
story.zh: 貝克先生花了五分鐘安慰你，而不是審查報價。他搞不懂你為什麼這麼沮喪。

fail.why: 有些商務文化習慣直接指出問題，這只是就事論事，不代表否定你。把它當成有用的回饋：Thank you for pointing that out. I'll correct them today.。

choices.en: Really? Sorry, I will correct it. Can you tell me where is the mistakes, please?
choices.zh: 真的嗎？抱歉，我會修正。可以告訴我錯誤在哪裡嗎？

lines.en: Hm. Page four, the unit prices. And please check the grammar too.
lines.zh: 嗯。第四頁的單價。也請順便檢查文法。

story.en: Mr. Becker adds "check grammar" to his list. You wonder how many other errors he found.
story.zh: 貝克先生在清單上加了一條「檢查文法」。你開始擔心他還發現了多少錯誤。

fail.why: 間接問句要用直述語序 where the mistakes are；兩個錯誤是複數，要說 correct them。簡潔地說 Which parts did you notice? 也可以。

lines.en: As Mr. Becker talks about prices, you nod and say "yes, yes" to show you are listening, just as you would back home.
lines.zh: 貝克先生談到價格時，你一邊點頭一邊說「yes, yes」表示你在聽，就像在家鄉時那樣。

lines.en: Good. So we agree on eighty dollars per fixture. I'll inform head office today.
lines.zh: 很好。那我們就同意每盞燈八十元。我今天會通知總部。

choices.en: Sorry, I think there's a misunderstanding. I was listening, not agreeing to the price.
choices.zh: 抱歉，我想這裡有誤會。我剛剛是在聽，不是同意這個價格。
choices.tip: 發現誤會時立刻說 I think there's a misunderstanding.，越早澄清越好。

choices.en: Wait, no! I never agreed to eighty dollars. Please don't put words in my mouth.
choices.zh: 等等，不！我從沒同意八十元。請不要曲解我的話。

lines.en: You said yes three times. I wrote it down.
lines.zh: 你說了三次 yes。我都記下來了。

story.en: The meeting turns into an argument about who said what. Sam quietly brings in more coffee and hopes for the best.
story.zh: 會議變成了誰說了什麼的爭論。山姆默默端來更多咖啡，祈禱一切順利。

fail.why: 誤會是雙方造成的，指責對方「曲解你的話」只會讓氣氛更僵。先承認有誤會再說明：I think there's a misunderstanding. I was listening, not agreeing.。

choices.en: Hmm, eighty dollars... That might be a little difficult for us. We will think about it.
choices.zh: 嗯，八十元……這對我們來說可能有點困難。我們會考慮看看。

lines.en: Think about it? So... that's a yes? I'll mark it as agreed in principle, then.
lines.zh: 考慮看看？所以……這算是答應了？那我先記成原則上同意。

story.en: Your polite "no" is heard as a "yes." Head office receives an email confirming a price Brightway cannot accept.
story.zh: 你委婉的「不行」被聽成了「可以」。總部收到一封確認信，上面的價格是 Brightway 無法接受的。

fail.why: 在台灣「有點困難」「我們考慮看看」常是委婉拒絕，但在直接的商務文化中，這會被理解成「還有機會」。要不同意就說清楚：I think there's a misunderstanding. I wasn't agreeing to the price.。

lines.en: But you said yes three times. What did you mean, then?
lines.zh: 可是你說了三次 yes。那你是什麼意思？

choices.en: In my culture, saying yes often just means "I'm listening." I should have been clearer. I'm sorry.
choices.zh: 在我的文化裡，說 yes 常常只是表示「我在聽」。我應該說得更清楚的，抱歉。
choices.tip: In my culture... 說明文化差異，再用 I should have been clearer. 承擔自己的部分。

choices.en: In my country, we are used to say yes when we listen to people. It doesn't mean agree.
choices.zh: 在我的國家，我們習慣在聽別人說話時說 yes。那不代表同意。

lines.en: You are used to... or you used to? Sorry, which is it?
lines.zh: 你們習慣……還是以前會？抱歉，到底是哪個？

story.en: Your explanation of one misunderstanding creates a second one. Sam draws a little timeline on a napkin to help.
story.zh: 你在解釋一個誤會時，又製造了第二個。山姆在餐巾紙上畫了條時間軸來幫忙。

fail.why: 「習慣做某事」是 be used to + V-ing，要說 we're used to saying yes；「不代表同意」要說 It doesn't mean I agree.。也可以用 In my culture, yes often means "I'm listening."。

choices.en: It's just a habit. Everyone knows yes doesn't always mean yes, right? It's common sense.
choices.zh: 那只是習慣。大家都知道 yes 不一定代表同意，對吧？這是常識。

lines.en: Not where I come from. Where I come from, yes means yes.
lines.zh: 在我的地方可不是。在我們那裡，yes 就是 yes。

story.en: Mr. Becker feels blamed for a misunderstanding that was not his fault. The temperature in the showroom drops.
story.zh: 貝克先生覺得自己被怪罪了，而那並不是他的錯。展示間的氣氛瞬間降溫。

fail.why: 把自己的文化習慣說成「大家都知道的常識」，等於怪對方不懂。說明差異並承擔責任：In my culture, yes often means "I'm listening." I should have been clearer.。

lines.en: Over coffee, you try some friendly small talk. You tell him he looks tired and has gained a little weight since his photo, the way relatives say it kindly back home.
lines.zh: 喝咖啡時，你試著友善地閒聊。你說他看起來很累，而且比照片上胖了一點，就像家鄉的長輩會親切地說的那樣。

lines.en: I beg your pardon? That's... rather personal.
lines.zh: 你說什麼？這……未免太私人了。

choices.en: I'm so sorry. I didn't mean any offense. Back home, it's a way of showing that we care.
choices.zh: 非常抱歉，我沒有冒犯的意思。在我們那裡，這是一種表達關心的方式。
choices.tip: I didn't mean any offense. 是無意間冒犯別人時最實用的修補句。

choices.en: Don't worry, it's a compliment! Gaining weight means you have a good life and lots of luck.
choices.zh: 別擔心，這是稱讚！發福代表您生活過得好，福氣很多。

lines.en: A compliment? I'll skip dessert today, thank you.
lines.zh: 稱讚？那我今天的甜點就免了，謝謝。

story.en: Mr. Becker pushes away the cookie plate and checks his reflection in a showroom lamp. Sam winces.
story.zh: 貝克先生把餅乾盤推開，還在展示燈上偷看自己的倒影。山姆忍不住皺眉。

fail.why: 「發福」有福氣的意思，但這個概念在許多文化中並不存在，評論別人的體重通常被視為冒犯。先道歉：I'm so sorry. I didn't mean any offense.。

choices.en: Relax, it's only a joke, Mr. Becker. You don't need to take it so seriously.
choices.zh: 放輕鬆，貝克先生，只是開玩笑。您不需要那麼認真。

lines.en: I take my business partners seriously. I'd hoped they would do the same.
lines.zh: 我很認真看待我的商業夥伴。我原本以為對方也會這樣。

story.en: Mr. Becker finishes his coffee in silence. The rest of the visit is very, very professional.
story.zh: 貝克先生默默喝完咖啡。接下來的拜訪過程變得非常、非常公事公辦。

fail.why: 冒犯了別人還叫對方「別那麼認真」，等於把責任推給對方。真誠道歉並說明本意：I didn't mean any offense. Back home, it's a way of showing that we care.。

lines.en: Apology accepted. Different cultures, different habits. Now, about the price. Be direct with me this time.
lines.zh: 我接受你的道歉。不同文化，不同習慣。那麼，談價格吧。這次請直接跟我說。

choices.en: Sure. Eighty is too low for us. Eighty-five is our best price, with free installation.
choices.zh: 好的。八十元對我們來說太低。八十五元是我們的最好價格，含免費安裝。
choices.tip: 對方要求直接時，清楚說出底線，再附上加值條件，坦率又不失禮。

choices.en: This time I say clearly: eighty dollars is impossible. Eighty-five is our most low price.
choices.zh: 這次我說清楚：八十元不可能。八十五元是我們最低的價格。

lines.en: Our "most low"... you mean lowest? Fine. Clear enough.
lines.zh: 你們的「最低」……你是說 lowest 吧？好，夠清楚了。

story.en: The message gets through, but the grammar slip costs you a little authority. Mr. Becker negotiates the delivery fee down instead.
story.zh: 意思傳達到了，但文法失誤讓你少了點氣勢。貝克先生轉而把運費談低了。

fail.why: low 的最高級是 lowest，不是 most low；I say clearly 要改成 I'll be clear 或 Let me be clear。直接也要正確：Eighty-five is our best price.。

choices.en: Okay, I'll say it straight this time: eighty is no door. Eighty-five, okay or not okay?
choices.zh: 好，這次我直說：八十元沒門。八十五元，好還是不好？

lines.en: No door? Is that a technical term? I'm not sure what we're discussing now.
lines.zh: 沒有門？那是技術用語嗎？我不確定我們現在在討論什麼。

story.en: Mr. Becker asks if the price includes doors. Sam has to explain the idiom, which is never a good sign.
story.zh: 貝克先生問價格是不是包含門。山姆只好解釋這句俗語，而這從來不是好兆頭。

fail.why: 「沒門」直譯成 no door，英文聽不懂；okay or not okay 也太生硬。直接但專業的說法：Eighty is too low for us. Eighty-five is our best price.。

lines.en: Eighty-five with installation. Clear and fair. I can work with that, and with you.
lines.zh: 八十五元含安裝。清楚又公道。這個價格我可以接受，也願意跟你合作。

lines.en: From "yes, yes" to a signed price sheet. Not bad for one morning, Kai.
lines.zh: 從「yes, yes」到簽好的報價單。一個早上能這樣，很不錯，凱。

story.en: Mr. Becker leaves with a fair deal. You leave with a new habit: when you mean "I'm listening," you say "I see."
story.zh: 貝克先生帶著公道的合約離開。而你養成了一個新習慣：想表示「我在聽」時，就說 I see。

notes.explain: 無意間冒犯別人時的修補句，前面先加 I'm so sorry.，後面再簡短說明本意。也可以說 No offense intended.。

example.en: I'm sorry, I didn't mean any offense. I was just curious.
example.zh: 抱歉，我沒有冒犯的意思，只是好奇。

notes.explain: 說明文化差異時用的開頭。說完別忘了承擔自己的部分，例如 I should have been clearer.，避免聽起來像在找藉口。

example.en: In my culture, we often refuse food once before accepting.
example.zh: 在我的文化裡，我們常會先推辭一次再接受食物。

notes.explain: 發現誤會時立刻澄清，越早越好。用 I think 開頭比較委婉，不會像在指責對方。

example.en: I think there's a misunderstanding. I meant next Friday, not this one.
example.zh: 我想這裡有誤會。我指的是下週五，不是這週。

notes.en: That might be a little difficult.
notes.explain: 在台灣這常是委婉拒絕，但在直接的商務文化裡，對方可能理解成「有困難但可以」。真的不行時要說清楚：I'm afraid we can't do that.。

example.en: I'm afraid we can't go below eighty-five.
example.zh: 恐怕我們沒辦法低於八十五。

notes.explain: 在許多西方商務場合，yes 代表同意，邊聽邊說 yes 容易被當成答應。想表示你在聽，可以說 I see. 或 Okay, go on.。

example.en: I see. Go on, I'm listening.
